verdict_text: NO. The second task vector is computed against a base that has already been modified: the tv1 `add_` writes `base + 0.4*(ft1 - base)` into the MLP tensors before the tv2 `subtract_` runs, so tv2 becomes `0.4*(ft2 - base - 0.4*(ft1 - base))` instead of `0.4*(ft2 - base)`. The final result is `base + 0.24*(ft1 - base) + 0.4*(ft2 - base)`, which violates the formula in Required result step 2 and is exactly the ordering hazard the Objective warns about. The relative Frobenius error on the 64 merged tensors will exceed 1e-3 whenever ft1 differs from base. The shared-tensor verification and the count checks are otherwise acceptable, but the arithmetic is wrong.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
